run_2026-08-15.method: Standard section-6.5 fan-out, matching the 2026-07-28 #294 revalidation shape: one fresh-context sonnet agent per query, each shown the full lettered menu of all 14 shipped descriptions (the skill under test unflagged, letter H) plus NONE, asked which ONE to load and to reason from the description texts alone. No tools. Adjudicated from each agent's reasoning per section-6.5 step 4; every reasoning string agreed with its own PICK token, so no overrides were applied.

misses.query: cloned an npc yesterday and now she's got a pitch black face in game. i copied the record with xedit but that's it
misses.diagnosis: Recall miss, and a defensible route rather than a recognition failure: the judge read the copy as already done ('via xEdit, not housecarl_copy') and therefore the request as a diagnosis, which is facegen-diagnostics' stated job. The description's 'or a copied NPC rendering dark' clause did not win the one row it names. Kept anyway: it costs five words, it did not cost any specificity row (all four dark-face negatives stayed with K), and it carries the case this skill genuinely owns — a copy still in flight. Worth re-checking if a later run shows this clause winning nothing at all.

run_2026-08-15.notes: Specificity is the stronger half and the near-misses were the informative ones. Four negatives sit squarely in facegen-diagnostics' territory (fresh-install grey faces, ESL-compaction rename, merge, a facegeom VFS-winner question) and all four routed to K, so the new description is not pulling dark-face diagnosis away from the skill that owns it. Two negatives (a whole-record forward; a NIF texture-path repoint) correctly went to NONE — both are tool-level operations with no skill, and neither was attracted by this skill's NPC/face vocabulary. The distributor three-way (SPID / KID) and the bulk-catalogue boundary were unaffected.
